answer: An atlas marketplace buying habitat maps of a meadow and ridge grants each agent one task slot per non-rehypothecatable bond, locked through audit. A public nullifier ties the bond to one slot per epoch without exposing the owner. Fifty aliases need fifty bonds and face fifty slashable audit risks; rotating independent reviewers compare submitted maps to withheld satellite samples. Rich attackers can still fund many bonds, and corrupt reviewers can collude, so this limits cheap cloning rather than proving one human per agent.
